tasks.short: Conduct cardiovascular treatment and prevention research

steps.what: Conduct research to develop or test cardiovascular medications, treatments and preventive procedures

tasks.design: Retain the cardiologist's research design, clinical conduct and interpretation, with protocol references in {DOCS}. Specific data-entry, analysis or report tasks need their own measured boundaries before proposing an additional saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical research depends on appropriate questions, credible observations and interpretation under uncertainty.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's clinical documentation and screening capabilities do not establish autonomous cardiovascular research.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing useful clinical evidence from bias, confounding and incomplete observations.
tasks.human_edge: The cardiologist judges clinical relevance and the implications for participants and future care.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in research responsibility, study permission or clinical judgement.

reach.task: Explain clinical uncertainties and protocol concerns
reach.learn: Protocol deviations and research evidence traceability

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical research conduct and interpretation remain human in this proposal; the supplied digest does not establish a cardiovascular research labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the cardiologist's own research work, excluding other researchers' labour and any separate documentation task. No research administration share is invented.

The cardiologist identifies protocol version, participant or analysis scope, relevant observations, deviations and uncertainty during s1. Capture and verification remain fully counted; no structured eligibility, valid-endpoint or successful-treatment flag is assumed.

Study observations are produced through the existing approved study process, with provenance checked by the cardiologist. Missing or contradictory evidence requires manual investigation rather than inferred values.
Use existing native research and document tools first. No additional process or integration is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Study types and the cardiologist's actual research duties
Whether repeatable data handling is separately measurable
research_questions: Can study time sampling isolate a repeatable data-handling burden without treating clinical research judgement as administration?

already_counted.description: Conduct and interpret the cardiologist's research work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine protocol work and unexpected clinical findings both retain full research judgement and conduct time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design and explain patient treatment plans

steps.what: Design treatment plans by integrating patient history, reports, examination results and preferences
Check and explain the proposed treatment plan, discussing choices and confirming the agreed approach

tasks.design: Keep treatment design and explanation with the cardiologist, supported by the patient record in {OTHER}. Existing medication surveillance can inform review, while the cardiologist determines applicability and discusses the actual choices with the patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: A treatment choice requires individual clinical reasoning and the patient's goals and preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rule checks support medication review but do not remove treatment planning or shared discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing benefits, contraindications, uncertainty and what the patient can realistically follow.
tasks.human_edge: The cardiologist can adapt the plan to the person's circumstances and resolve conflicting clinical considerations.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in treatment authority or patient discussion time.

reach.task: Explain the agreed plan and unresolved follow-up questions

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard provides interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate checks; these are support capabilities rather than autonomous treatment-plan design.
Model knowledge: patient-specific treatment planning and explanation retain full clinical and conversation time in this proposal.

assumptions: Boundary is designing and explaining the treatment plan, excluding separate diagnosis, prescription entry, documentation and subsequent care execution.

OTHER means the clinical patient record. The cardiologist verifies patient identity, relevant history, current medication evidence, test provenance, clinical findings and patient preferences during s1. All reconciliation and capture remain counted; no free structured contraindication or suitability flag is assumed.

The patient supplies preferences and questions in the consultation. Uncertain history, inconsistent results or unresolved medication information require manual clarification before agreement, not inferred values.
Use existing native record and surveillance functions. No new rule set, generated plan or integration is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
If the plan explanation also satisfies the separate general procedure-discussion task, the shared conversation must be assigned once in a roll-up.
unknowns: Existing clinical record and surveillance coverage
Overlap between plan explanation and other patient-discussion tasks
research_questions: Is any repeat plan documentation distinct from the clinical decisions and explanation measured here?

already_counted.description: Integrate clinical evidence and discuss and agree the plan

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient-specific treatment plan and clinical context checked before agreement and communication; clinical changes require reassessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. A straightforward follow-up plan and competing treatment choices both retain full clinical design and patient explanation time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose cardiovascular conditions from clinical evidence

steps.what: Diagnose patients' medical conditions by reconciling records, reports, test results and examination findings

tasks.design: Retain diagnostic reconciliation and judgement with the cardiologist, using the clinical record in {OTHER}. This proposal does not extend a screening or record-drafting capability into an autonomous cardiovascular diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagnosis requires relating uncertain or conflicting findings to the individual clinical presentation.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied digest does not demonstrate removal of cardiologist diagnostic judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising atypical disease, incomplete evidence and results that do not fit the apparent explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The cardiologist can revise a differential and seek further evidence when a plausible answer is inadequate.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in diagnostic responsibility or authority.

reach.task: Clarify which test finding needs further verification

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: cardiovascular diagnosis from mixed clinical evidence remains the cardiologist's judgement; the supplied digest does not establish a task labour reduction.

assumptions: Boundary is the cardiologist's diagnostic interpretation, excluding acquisition of tests, treatment-plan design and separate record drafting.

OTHER means the clinical patient record. The cardiologist checks identity, encounter, source and test dates, units, findings, conflicts and diagnostic uncertainty within s1. Capture and reconciliation remain fully counted.

Test staff produce the original results in the existing care process. No free structured diagnosis, normality or data-completeness flag is assumed; uncertain provenance or conflicting findings require manual verification.
Existing native records and test viewers remain in use. No new diagnostic system, model or integration is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual diagnostic case mix and existing specialised tools
research_questions: Is there measurable repetitive result retrieval distinct from the diagnostic judgement itself?

already_counted.description: Reconcile clinical evidence and determine or qualify the diagnosis

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient encounter, reconciled evidence and diagnosis or differential recorded after clinical assessment; new evidence requires reassessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Clear follow-up findings and an uncertain differential both retain full diagnostic interpretation time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain procedures, results and treatments to patients

steps.what: Explain procedures and discuss results or treatments, answering patients' questions and checking understanding

tasks.design: Retain the patient conversation and understanding check with the cardiologist, supported by the checked clinical record in {OTHER}. General information sheets may support a discussion but do not replace explanation of this patient's findings or choices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients need an explanation that responds to their concerns and actual understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted public information exists, but its availability does not demonstrate shorter individual clinical discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertainty and sensitive findings in language the patient understands.
tasks.human_edge: The cardiologist can notice confusion, respond to emotion and adapt the explanation.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in patient-discussion responsibility or time.

reach.task: Communicate unresolved patient concerns for follow-up

evidence.claim: Thuisarts provides guideline-based public health information; this supports general reference material rather than replacement of a cardiologist's patient-specific conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is the cardiologist's explanation and discussion, excluding diagnosis, leaflet production and separate documentation. A conversation shared with treatment-plan explanation must be assigned once in a roll-up.

OTHER means the clinical patient record. The cardiologist checks the relevant result or plan version and identifies the patient's questions, language needs and understanding during s1. That work remains fully counted; no structured patient-understands flag is assumed.

Clinical findings come from the existing diagnostic process and are checked for this encounter; the patient supplies questions during the discussion. Unclear evidence or misunderstanding requires manual clarification and further explanation.
Use existing native patient information and record access. No new generated explanation or integration is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How discussion overlaps with treatment planning
research_questions: Does a time sample identify any separate repeat preparation without reducing patient question and understanding time?

already_counted.description: Explain clinical information, answer questions and check understanding

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine result explanation and a distressed patient's detailed questions both retain full discussion and understanding-check time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical research, diagnosis, treatment design and patient understanding remain fully counted; separate documentation aids require their own task boundary.
reach: Give research coordinators precise clinical uncertainties
Help nurses follow up unresolved patient concerns
role.ambitious_version: A cardiologist whose clinical judgement and patient conversations remain resourced while any later documentation improvements are measured separately.
